questions.question: Let $C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be convex and $f\colon C\to\mathbb{R}$. Which condition defines convexity of $f$, for every $x,y\in C$ and $\lambda\in[0,1]$?
options: $f(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y)\ge\lambda f(x)+(1-\lambda)f(y)$
$f(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y)\le\max\{f(x),f(y)\}$
$f(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y)=\lambda f(x)+(1-\lambda)f(y)$
$f(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y)\le\lambda f(x)+(1-\lambda)f(y)$

questions.question: Let $u\colon\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be concave and define $c(x)=-u(-x)$. Which conclusion follows?
options: $c$ is concave because reflecting the input preserves concavity
$c$ is convex because output negation reverses the concavity inequality
$c$ is affine because the two minus signs cancel
$c$ need not be convex because input reflection destroys concavity

questions.question: For a convex function $f\colon C\to\mathbb{R}$, the convexity inequality is imposed for all $x,y\in C$ and $\lambda\in[0,1]$. Why must $C$ be convex?
options: So that every point $\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y$ lies in $C$
So that $f$ attains a minimum somewhere on $C$
So that $f$ is continuous at every point of $C$
So that $f$ is bounded on the whole set $C$

questions.question: Let $f$ be convex on a convex set $C$. Suppose $p,q\in C$ satisfy $f(p)=3$ and $f(q)=1$. Could $p$ be a local minimiser relative to $C$?
options: Yes, if $q$ is sufficiently far from $p$
Yes, provided $f$ is convex but not strictly convex
No: nearby points towards $q$ have smaller values
Yes, if $p$ lies on the boundary of $C$

questions.question: A strictly convex function $f\colon\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfies $f(p)=f(q)=m$ at distinct points $p$ and $q$. Could both points be global minimisers?
options: Yes: equal function values are sufficient for both points to be minimisers
No: their midpoint has value strictly below $m$
Yes: strict convexity permits several global minimisers if each is isolated
Yes: strict convexity only rules out local minimisers

questions.question: For $f(x,y)=x^2+y^2$, $x=(1,0)$, $y=(-1,2)$ and $\lambda=\tfrac{1}{2}$, what are the left side $f(\tfrac{1}{2}x+\tfrac{1}{2}y)$ and the right side $\tfrac{1}{2}f(x)+\tfrac{1}{2}f(y)$ of the convexity inequality?
Is $f(x,y)=xy$ convex on $\mathbb{R}^2$?
options: No: along $(t,-t)$ it equals $-t^2$
Yes, as it is linear in each variable separately
Yes, as every polynomial is convex
No, as it takes negative values

questions.question: Which of these functions is concave on $(0,\infty)^2$?
options: $\mathrm{e}^{x+y}$
$\log x+\log y$
$xy$

questions.question: If $f$ and $g$ are convex on $\mathbb{R}^n$, which function need not be convex?
options: $f+g$
$\max(f,g)$
$f-g$

questions.question: For $h(x,y)=2x-3y+4$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$, which classification follows from the convexity and concavity inequalities?
options: Convex, but it fails the concavity inequality
Both convex and concave
Concave only, because of the negative coefficient of $y$
Neither, since an affine graph has no curvature

questions.question: Let $n\ge2$ be an integer and let $f\colon\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$. Which collection of one-variable checks is equivalent to convexity of $f$?
options: Convexity in each coordinate separately, with the other coordinates fixed arbitrarily
Convexity on each coordinate axis through the origin
Convexity of $t\mapsto f(p+td)$ on $\mathbb{R}$ for every $p,d\in\mathbb{R}^n$
The inequality $f(p)\ge f(0)$ for every $p\in\mathbb{R}^n$

questions.question: Let $f\colon C\to\mathbb{R}$ be convex on a convex set $C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$, and let $x,y,z\in C$. How does $f((x+y+z)/3)$ compare with $(f(x)+f(y)+f(z))/3$?
options: It is at most that average
It is at least that average
The two are always equal
No comparison is possible for three points

questions.question: Is the Euclidean norm $f(x)=\|x\|$ convex on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and is it strictly convex?
options: Neither convex nor strictly convex
Strictly convex, just like $\|x\|^2$
Concave, since its graph is a cone
Convex, but not strictly convex

questions.question: Decide whether $g(x,y)=(x-2y+1)^2$ is a convex function on $\mathbb{R}^2$.
options: No, since it vanishes on a whole line
Yes: $t^2$ composed with an affine map
Only on the half-plane $x-2y+1\ge0$
No, since its Hessian is singular

questions.question: $f(x)=x$ and $g(x)=x^2$ are convex on $\mathbb{R}$. Is their product $f g$ convex on $\mathbb{R}$?
options: Yes: products of convex functions are convex
Yes, since $x^3$ is an increasing function
No: $x^3$ is concave on $(-\infty,0)$
No, since $x^3$ takes negative values

questions.question: A concave function $f$ on $[0,1]$ has $f(0)=2$ and $f(1)=5$. What is the smallest value of $f$ on $[0,1]$?
options: $2$, attained at $x=0$
Some value below $2$, inside the interval
$3.5$, the average of the end values
It cannot be determined from these data

questions.question: Let $f\colon\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$. If every sublevel set $\{x\in\mathbb{R}\colon f(x)\le c\}$, for $c\in\mathbb{R}$, is convex, must $f$ be convex?
options: Yes, by the definition of convexity
Yes, provided $f$ is continuous
No: $f(x)=\sqrt{|x|}$ is a counterexample
Yes, provided every nonempty sublevel set is bounded

questions.question: For $f\colon\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, define its epigraph $E=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\colon t\ge f(x)\}$. When is $E$ a convex set?
options: Convexity of $E$ requires all graph points to lie on a single affine plane
Convexity of $E$ follows from continuity, since each vertical ray has no gaps
Convexity of $E$ requires strict convexity, since boundary segments are forbidden
Convex combinations stay in $E$ exactly when $f$ satisfies the convexity inequality

questions.question: For which real $a$ is $f(x,y)=\mathrm{e}^x+\mathrm{e}^y+axy$ convex on $\mathbb{R}^2$?
options: Only $a=0$
Exactly $|a|\le1$
Exactly $|a|\le2$
Every $a$, as $\mathrm{e}^x$ and $\mathrm{e}^y$ are convex

questions.question: A convex function $f\colon\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfies $f(0,0)=1$, $f(2,0)=7$ and $f(0,2)=5$. What is the smallest possible value of $f(3,-1)$?
options: There is no finite lower bound
